summary: Pinned model unexpectedly overridden after canary snapshot replace leading to degraded-model fallback
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Packetly reported a burst of 5xx+degraded model responses for a handful of tenants immediately after a scheduled canary snapshot replace. Affected tenants had explicit pinned versions; however several requests were routed to the degraded quantized variant for ~3-6 minutes before pins were restored.

Impact:
- Intermittent incorrect model outputs for ~12 tenants (multi-tenant Dedicated pool) for ~3-6 minutes during the canary snapshot replace event.
- Customer-facing errors and quality regressions; one customer integration aborted batch jobs.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity pool: dc-09 (us-east), prod control-plane.
- Rolling canary snapshot replace performed by Platform Team between 2026-03-10 02:15-02:40 UTC.
- Affected pinned version: redwood-open-7b-v1 pinned by tenant policy. Fallback model: redwood-open-7b-degraded-quant (lower-precision fallback).

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Start a canary snapshot replace (orchestrator snapshot swap: new snapshot index published, orchestrator applies new mapping).
2) During the snapshot commit window, perform a pin commit/refresh for a tenant (pin was valid before snapshot).
3) Edge prewarm probes and sidecar index refresh race with control-plane snapshot commit, leading to a stale routing index at some edge nodes.
4) Traffic routed from those edge nodes bypasses pin mapping and falls back to routing rules that allow degraded-quant variant.

Observed logs / traces (excerpts):
- edge-proxy@edge-42: "routing-index: load v=20260310-02:15, pin-check: cache-miss, route=fallback-degraded-quant"
- orchestrator@dc-09: "snapshot-replace: commit-window=2026-03-10T02:16:12Z -> 02:16:30Z; published index id=20260310-216"
- control-plane@api: "pin-commit tenant=packetly-42 model=redwood-open-7b-v1 status=applied node=cp-11"
- serving-runtime@gpu-7: "model-variant-selection: pin not found in local-index -> choose fallback redwood-open-7b-degraded-quant"

Initial hypothesis:
- Snapshot index swap created a short period (tens of seconds) where edge nodes served requests with a newly loaded index that had not yet merged pin-affinity mappings originating from the control-plane pin-commit. The result was a transient routing window where local routing favored fallback variants.

Investigation notes:
- SRE reproduction: We ran a controlled canary-snapshot-swap in staging with pinned tenants and reproduced a 30-90s window where a subset of edge replicas reported pin-cache misses.
- Sidecar index refresh logs show TTLs differing between control-plane push and edge local merge (edge local merge lagged by ~12s).
- Observed correlation with ongoing edge prewarm probe traffic: prewarm created a hot path that loaded new index earlier than pin data propagated, causing mis-ordered index state.
- Control-plane pin-commit acknowledged as applied, but the index serialization used by edge merging did not include the newest pin-affinity records until the next index snapshot was produced (~3-6 minutes for some replicas under load).
- No evidence of database write failures or dropped control-plane acknowledgements. This appears to be a snapshot-merge ordering problem between pin-affinity table and routing-index publication.
investigation_notes: Reproducer run in staging: canary-snapshot-replace + simultaneous pin-commit -> 30-90s of misrouted requests on ~15% of edge replicas. Root cause suspected: index publish ordering + edge-merge race. Observed TTl mismatch between pin-affinity publish time and routing-index availability on edge. Edge prewarm probe traffic amplified the window by forcing early index loads. Metrics: pin-cache-miss spike aligns with snapshot commit timestamp. No GPU oom or autoscale events correlated. Logs saved to S3: s3://redwood-support/incidents/SUP-654321/trace-bundles/
comments: 2026-03-10 03:05 UTC - Aisha Patel (Support): Notified customer of incident and requested traces and example request IDs. Asked Platform team to pause non-urgent canary snapshot replaces for the dedicated pool.

2026-03-10 04:20 UTC - Jun Park (SRE): Reproduced in staging. Confirmed pin-cache miss on subset of edges during snapshot replace. Captured merge-order logs. Linking reproduction run: github.com/redwood/tests/PR/642.

2026-03-10 06:10 UTC - Platform Eng (Roberto Diaz): Identified index pub sequence: routing-index published before pin-affinity delta in the same maintenance window. Preparing patch to ensure pin-affinity is included in the atomic index snapshot or sequencing is adjusted.

2026-03-10 09:00 UTC - Support (Aisha): Applied customer-facing workaround: reapply tenant pin and request a rolling revalidate (pin-refresh) for affected tenants. Customer reported immediate improvement after pin refreshes.
2026-03-11 11:45 UTC - Product (Emily Zhang): Suggested adding a pre-snapshot quiesce step for edge prewarm traffic to reduce index-load races during maintenance windows.

2026-03-12 14:20 UTC - Jun Park (SRE): Preparing hotfix PR to control index publish ordering; will coordinate with Platform for staged rollout and additional monitoring alert for pin-cache-miss spikes.
resolution: Workaround applied: manual pin-refresh for affected tenants restored correct routing within 1-2 minutes. Temporary operational mitigation: paused non-critical snapshot replaces on dc-09 until sequencing patch is deployed. Permanent fix: orchestration patch to ensure pin-affinity deltas are atomically included in snapshot index (or ensure index merge ordering guarantees). Hotfix PR created: github.com/redwood/orchestrator/PR/412. Plan: staged rollout to dc-09, add alert for pin-cache-miss > 0.5% over 1 minute.
next_steps: 1) Push fix to orchestrator to enforce atomic pin-affinity inclusion in published index (PR linked). 2) Add a short quiesce of prewarm probes during snapshot commit window. 3) Add metric + pager alert for pin-cache-miss and snapshot-commit-rate. 4) Run controlled canary in staging with prewarm traffic and confirm no misroute window. 5) Postmortem to be drafted and shared with customer and #support channel.
impact_summary: Transient model-quality regressions and 5xx errors for a small set of enterprise tenants in us-east during a scheduled canary snapshot replace. Customer operational impact: aborted batch jobs and degraded responses for ~3-6 minutes. No data loss or model correctness drift beyond routing to known degraded variant.
follow_up_actions: ENG: Merge and stage orchestrator sequencing fix (PR 412)
SRE: Add pin-cache-miss alert and dashboard tile
DOCS: Update maintenance runbook to include prewarm quiesce
CS: Communicate RCA + timeline to affected customers
